subject: Finly discovery recap — latency & concurrency needs (p95 / streaming)
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
To: Jessica Park <jessica@finly.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 14 Apr 2026 15:05:00 -0700
Subject: Finly discovery recap — latency & concurrency needs (p95 / streaming)

Hey Jessica / Martin — thanks again for the call today. Quick recap from our side and a proposed set of next steps so we can move to a tech deep-dive next week.

Key pain points you shared
- Streaming UX feels choppy at scale: partial tokens arrive intermittently, causing the frontend spinner to pause for noticeable intervals.
- p95 token/partial latency spikes leading to poor perceived responsiveness.
- When concurrency climbs above ~300 active streams, overall throughput drops and 502s/timeout retries increase.

Current stack (high level) you mentioned
- Model hosting: self-managed GPUs in Azure (NV4s cluster) running a custom streaming proxy.
- Inference model: a LLM-based assistant (13B-ish equivalent) optimized with quantization but not a memory-optimized serving kernel.
- Frontend: streaming client that expects frequent small partials to show live typing.

Success criteria you called out
- Streaming perceived latency: p95 partial-token arrival < 200ms (goal: <150ms)
- End-to-end p95 generation for short responses (<64 tokens) < 400ms
- Sustained concurrency: 500+ concurrent active streams per region with <1% error rate and graceful degradation if capacity is exceeded
- Deterministic fallbacks: predictable routing to a lower-cost variant without breaking UX

What we heard as blockers
- Current serving stack defaults to larger batch sizes at peak, increasing p95 for streaming short responses
- KV cache / warm-start not fully leveraged so repeated sessions re-generate more context than necessary

Next steps (proposed)
1) Technical deep-dive (30–45m) next week with your infra/eng lead to review traffic shape and sample traces.
2) We run a short benchmark: you provide a representative traffic sample (1000 requests, typical prompt mix), we run 3 configurations (hosted default, dedicated with streaming-optimized kernels, and dedicated + prefix caching) and share p50/p95/p99 for token arrival and end-to-end.
3) Quick mutual action plan and pricing sketch if benchmarks meet your p95 targets.

Attachments: redwood-discovery-notes.pdf (summary), redwood-performance-playbook.pdf (how we tune streaming workloads)

If that aligns, I can send a calendar invite for the deep-dive and a short checklist of artifacts we need (sample traffic, representative prompts, current trace/metrics).

Thanks,
Marissa
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.ai | (415) 555-0123

From: Jessica Park <jessica@finly.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
Cc: Martin Lopez <mlopez@finly.com>
Date: Wed, 15 Apr 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Finly discovery recap — latency & concurrency needs (p95 / streaming)

Thanks Marissa — this is helpful and accurate. A few clarifications from our side:

- Current observed numbers: for short interactions (single-turn, ~20–60 tokens) our measured p95 end-to-end generation latency is around 650–800ms in production; partial-token arrival for streaming shows p95 ~420ms which makes the UX feel sluggish.
- Concurrency: our ingress load balancer starts to queue/overflow at ~300 simultaneous active streams per region (we're seeing request queueing and then retries).
- Stack specifics: Azure NV4s with 4–8 GPUs behind a custom scaling layer. Our streaming implementation opens a websocket per user and expects frequent small partials. We have some caching at the request layer but not persistent KV warm caches across sessions.

Our internal success criteria (prioritized):
1) Perceived streaming responsiveness: p95 partial-token latency < 200ms (stretch goal <150ms)
2) Stable behavior at 500 concurrent active streams per region with <1% failures
3) Reasonable cost per user — we need a model that keeps unit costs predictable.

We're happy to set up the traffic sample export and a 30-minute infra deep-dive with our engineering lead (Martin). How does Thu 2026-04-16 10:00 PT look?

-Jessica
Head of Product Engineering | Finly
jessica@finly.com

I'll attach the Redwood performance playbook which outlines the streaming-focused knobs we'll test. If benchmarks show p95 partial-token latency <200ms and sustained behavior at 500 concurrent streams, we can move to a pilot Dedicated plan with a short initial commit to validate in your environment.

Action items for you

- Share any SLOs / non-functional reqs we should be aware of (data retention, regional constraints).

Marissa
